literal: Unwashed foot inside the bed having placed is like, noble people's assembly a fool entering.
translation: A fool entering the assembly of the noble is like stepping onto a clean bed with unwashed feet.
modern: கழுவாத காலைப் படுக்கையினுள் வைப்பதைப் போன்றது, சான்றோர்களின் அவையினுள் அறிவிலி நுழைவது.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid everyday analogy to illustrate the discordance of ignorance in a refined setting. Entering a clean bed with dirty, unwashed feet instantly soils and ruins the purity of the sleeping space. Similarly, when an ignorant person enters an assembly of wise and noble scholars, their presence and unrefined behavior disrupt the intellectual harmony of the gathering. The poet highlights that a fool's intrusion is not just out of place, but actively defiles the dignity of a noble space.
